summary: Specifies how neighboring ATM label switching routers tell each other VCID values for their virtual connections when using LDP. This lets both ends agree on which circuit is which. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Two neighbors need to agree on which numbered pipe between them they mean. This is how they tell each other.

questions: how does ldp work over atm
why are vpi and vci not enough for ldp
subtitle: How neighbouring ATM label switching routers agree on a shared identifier for each virtual connection.

tldr.problem: On ATM links the VPI and VCI labels can be rewritten at every switch, so they cannot name a virtual connection in LDP label mapping messages.
tldr.mechanism: A Virtual Connection Identifier (VCID) has the same value at both ends of a VC. The upstream node proposes it and the downstream node acknowledges it, either inband on the VC or through ATM signaling, depending on the type of link.
tldr.outcome: LDP can refer to ATM VCs unambiguously. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 7274.

today: RFC 3038 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 7274. It defines how ATM-LSRs exchange VCID values for LDP.

sections.title: Why a VC Identifier Is Needed
sections.content:
An ATM Label Switching Router (ATM-LSR) applies label switching to ATM. In label switching, streams of packets are bound to layer 2 labels, and those bindings are passed between peers by the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP, RFC 3036).

On an ATM link the labels are the VPI and VCI of a virtual connection (VC). In the general case they are rewritten with new values at every switch the VC passes through, so they cannot identify a VC end to end in LDP mapping messages. The RFC introduces the Virtual Connection Identifier (VCID), which has the same value at both ends of a VC, and specifies the procedures neighbouring ATM-LSRs use to exchange it.
sections.eli5: A pipe can get a new label at every junction, so the two ends cannot just use the label. They need a name that does not change.

sections.title: Which Procedure Applies to Which Link
sections.content:
The procedures fall into two groups. Inband procedures send the notification messages over the VC they describe. Outband procedures send them over some other connection.

The choice depends on the type of VC. A transparent point-to-point link has the same VPI/VCI at both ends, so no notification is needed. A VP can use inband notification, VPID notification, or none if the node has only one VP to the neighbour (the VCI can then serve as the VCID). A PVC uses inband notification. An SVC has three options: carry the VCID directly in a signaling field large enough to hold it (such as the GIT of RFC 3033), use a small signaling field, or use inband notification when signaling cannot carry user information.

A VC has a direction, and the procedure is always triggered by the upstream node, which tells the downstream node the VCID. A bidirectional VC needs two procedures, one per direction. VC directionality is communicated through LDP.
sections.eli5: How the two ends tell each other the name depends on what kind of pipe it is. Some pipes already look the same from both ends, so they need no name at all.

sections.title: Inband Notification
sections.content:
For a point-to-point VC, node A first establishes the VC to node B and picks a VCID. A sends a VCID PROPOSE message with the VCID and a message ID through the new VC, and associates its outgoing label (VPI/VCI) with the VCID. B associates the VCID with its incoming label and, until it receives the LDP Request message, discards everything on the VC except the PROPOSE message. B replies with an ACK carrying the same VCID and message ID.

If A gets an ACK whose VCID and message ID match, it regards B as having made the association. Otherwise the message is ignored, and if no matching ACK arrives within a given period, A resends the PROPOSE. A then sends an LDP Request containing the PROPOSE message ID, and B answers with an LDP Mapping message carrying the VCID in the label TLV.

The PROPOSE, ACK and LDP Request exchange is a 3-way handshake. It is required because transmission of the PROPOSE message is unreliable. Once it completes, B ignores any further PROPOSE messages on that VC.

The RFC also defines the procedure for point-to-multipoint VCs, for future use because the LDP specification of the time did not support multicast. The upstream node sends the PROPOSE to all leaves, and the same VCID is reused when a leaf is added to an existing VC. A downstream node that has already received the LDP Request discards the message.
sections.eli5: One side says here is the name I picked, the other says got it, and then the first side says okay, now let us talk about this pipe. Three short messages make sure both really heard.

sections.title: Outband Notification and VPID
sections.content:
When a VC is set up with ATM signaling and the signaling message has a field too small for a VCID, the small-sized field method is used. The SETUP message of ATM Forum UNI 3.1/4.0 has a 7-bit user-specific field in the layer 3 protocol field of the BLLI information element. Its value serves as a temporary identifier for the VC during notification. The upstream LSR sends a VCID PROPOSE pairing the BLLI value with the VCID, the downstream LSR acknowledges, and the BLLI value is then free for reuse. A BLLI value must not be given to another VC while a procedure is in progress, and the receiver must recognise both the BLLI value and the sender address, because BLLI values are only unique at the sender.

If a signaling field such as GIT is large enough, the VCID is carried directly in the signaling message and the node simply follows with the LDP Request and Mapping messages.

VPID notification applies the same approach to share an identifier for a whole VP, once per direction. Afterwards a VC's VCID is built from the VPID as the most significant part and the VCI as the least significant part, so no per-VC notification is required. For VPID messages, both nodes use VCI=33 on a bidirectional VC. On a unidirectional VC the node with the larger LDP Identifier uses VCI=33 and the other uses VCI=34. VCI=32, used for unlabeled packet transfer, is not used here.
sections.eli5: If the pipe-setup note has only a tiny space, a short nickname is written there first, and then the real number is sent. For a whole bundle of pipes, one number covers them all.

sections.title: VCID Message Formats
sections.content:
A VCID message is the LDP fixed header followed by one or more TLVs. The inband VCID PROPOSE and the VPID PROPOSE are sent as null encapsulation packets, with only a label stack header before the LDP PDU, and the label value in that entry is 4. That reserved label is needed because, on a point-to-multipoint VC, a downstream node may receive the message after it has already received the LDP Label Request, and must tell the PROPOSE apart and ignore it. The other messages are sent as TCP packets, as in LDP.

The message types run from 0x0501 to 0x0507. ACK and NACK messages echo the VCID and carry the message ID of the PROPOSE they answer in a VCID Message ID field.

The TLVs are the VCID Label TLV (0x0203) with a 4-byte VCID, the VCID Message ID TLV (0x0701) with a 4-byte value, the VCID Temporary ID TLV (0x0702) holding the BLLI value, and the VPID TLV (0x0703) with a 2-byte VPID.
sections.eli5: Each kind of note has its own code number at the top so the reader knows what it is, and the notes use a special stamp so they are not mistaken for ordinary mail.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says the document does not introduce new security issues beyond those present in LDP, and that the same mechanisms proposed for that technology may be used. It gives no additional security mechanisms of its own.
sections.eli5: This note adds no new dangers beyond the ones the main system already has.
